Subject: 16 Lateral Design
Comment: ASCE 7-10 12.12.5 Deformation Compatibility for Seismic Design Categories D through F. For structures assigned to Seismic Design Category D, E, or F, every structural component not included in the seismic force-resisting system in the direction under consideration shall be designed to be adequate for the gravity load effects and the seismic forces resulting from displacement caused by the design story drift ( Δ)as determined in accordance with Section 12.8.6 (see also Section 12.12.1). The tension rods appear to be designed for the seismic forces (7.4k) associated with just the building and not in conjunction with the seismic loading of the soldier pile wall (S5.0).  When the soldier pile wall deflects 0.71" in a seismic event, the tension rod will elongate by nearly an inch.  This deformation will exceed the tensile capacity of the 36ksi, 1" diameter rod.  Please resize the rod to be compatible with the displacement created by the soldier pile's tip deflection.Structural Engineer (2)

Subject: 16 Lateral Design
Comment: ASCE 7-10 12.14.7.3 Collector Elements.  Collector elements shall be provided with adequate strength to transfer the seismic forces originating in other portions of the structure to the element providing the resistance to those forces (Fig. 12.10-1). Collector elements, splices, and their connections to resisting elements shall be designed to resist the forces de ﬁned in Section12.14.3.2. From the SST catalog, it doesn't appear that there is information for in-plane connection capacity for seismic loads (from the collector beams) to the ECCLQ column cap (15/S5.0).  Please provide structural design sizing such that the transfer for forces from the beam to the proprietary cap doesn't exceed bolt or SDS screw capacity or specify connection hardware with published in-plane collector capacities. w  SC  EA

This project includes new roof area and pervious pavement/pavers that add up to more than 1500 square feet.  Projects with more than 1500sf of new and replaced hard surface are required to provide On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) in accordance with the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual. The required process for OSM best management practice selection is described in Section 3.3 of Volume 3. The following documents have been prepared to comply with the requirements. These documents are available at http://www.seattle.gov/DPD/codesrules/codes/stormwater/default.htm.  All documents need to use the latest templates available.  Standard details for OSM facilities are available on the Stormwater Code webpage at http://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code under "Forms and Documents". You are not required to use the templates, but the submitted plans will need to include all of the relevant information included in the templates.  See Section 8.2 of Volume 1 of the Stormwater Manual for more information on minimum submittal requirements. a) Standard Construction Stormwater Control and Soil Amendment Plan (submitted) b) Standard Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan (submitted) c) On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) Calculator.

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: CORRECTION This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070, Standards for vegetation and impervious surface management. The related project activities are located within the mapped landslide prone environmentally critical area. Revegetation requirements apply within ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity.  The construction permit application will need to demonstrate compliance with SMC 25.09.070. The following information must be included in your permit application materials so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated on sheets L1, L2, DWC and CSC/Soil   A. Update EXISTING ground coverage conditions on landscape/site plan and table (L1): a. The area in square feet of temporary construction disturbance activity; b. The area in square feet of permanent new hard surface ground disturbed; and c. The total hard surface to remain. d. Use this calculation for total area of impact that requires mitigation. (a+b) - c = d  - Provide a brief description of the EXISTING ground coverage within these areas. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping, blackberry or other invasive species, trees, patio, pathway. Please specify the number of trees to be removed within ECAs and their buffers (if any), including their species, size, and health. B. Based on existing ground coverage, please show/delineate the PROPOSED mitigation  in the form of replanting on the landscape/site plan and table (L2): - The location, size, species, quantities and spacing of trees/shrubs to be removed and newly planted per calculation on ECA standard mitigation plan . - New trees must be two gallon size and shrubs one gallon.  - No permanent irrigation is allowed in mapped ECA steep slope erosion hazard areas or their buffers.  - Planting selections shall be native species suited to specific site conditions/orientation, no cultivars. It appears you will need to replace the following with native plant species. Amelanchier, Digitalis, Huechera, Thymus and Vinca.  - Add a note that areas that have been cleared, graded, or compacted are to be amended with organic matter prior to planting.  - Clearly delineate the entire site is as "Potential Slide Area (ECA2). The SDCI External GIS Map  https://seattlecitygis.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=f822b2c6498c4163b0 cf908e2241e9c2  is a helpful tool to locate designated steep slopes on the lot (20%). C. Site plan existing and proposed (L1 and L2), CSC and DWC: Show locations of all existing trees (per arborist report) on and off  the site and include a tree table with tree genus, species, common name, DBH (diameter at breast height), dripline for all existing trees and identify trees proposed for removal and/or retention.Revegetation (2)

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: D. Mitigation is required for lost ecological function when trees and vegetation are removed within the ECAs. You may need to relocate and/or reconfigure structures and/or utilities to avoid tree and vegetation removal. If necessary update the table on the existing landscape/site plan of existing trees and delineate those retained, removed, and if located in an ECA. For tree(s) that are proposed for removal, an assessment is required of the tree(s) as high risk and mitigation equal to the canopy removed per (SMC) 25.09.070.F. Reference TIP 331B page 2 for the tree risk assessment form and required professional that completes it. https://www.seattle.gov/DPD/Publications/CAM/cam331b.pdfNoteProvide  Provide consistency making sure tree locations and number identifiers match the arborist report.   E. Include a brief summary of the existing ecological functions performed by the ECA on and adjacent to the site. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration. F. SDCI requires that you demonstrate the use of required mitigation sequencing in the project development phase (SMC 25.09.065.B.1). These required steps are meant to find the least environmentally- damaging practicable alternative to achieve a project need. Further, provide an analysis detailing how the specific existing ecological functions impacted will be mitigated (SMC 25.09.070.G.2.b). Mitigation measures generally include improving the function(s) within the remaining ECA through native vegetation planting, drainage improvements, soil amendment, stormwater features (e.g., vegetated roof, Green Factor elements, bioretention planters, etc.). Provide an analysis as to why they will be adequate to mitigate for adverse impacts on ecological functions, if any.

Comment: 11. WALL PANEL CALCULATIONS CYCLE #1: Pages WL-9 through WL-12 of calculations appear to show wall lengths and/or locations that are not consistent with plan set. Revise calculations to show wall lengths and locations consistent with calculations, or explain why the inconsistencies are appropriate. Some examples for inconsistencies for Level 1 (page WL-9) are listed below - similar inconsistencies appear for other levels.      A. wall lengths: WP19, WP112, and WP144       B. wall locations: WP6 and WP145  CYCLE #2: Some wall lengths still don't match plans.  Example 1: Level 1, WP26 is longer in analysis than on plan.  Example 2: Level 4, WP926A shown in calculations, but missing on plans Engineer to review and revise calculations and/or plans to show consistent shear wall lengths and locations. CYCLE #3:  Some discrepancies between plans and calculations still exist. It appears that the horizontal distribution of shear is highly dependent on the lengths, locations, and stiffnesses of wood shear walls. Below are some observed concerns. Revise plans and/or calculations to resolve the inconsistencies or provide explanation why the inconsistencies are appropriate or trivial.      A. Holdowns for some shear walls are not located at the end of the shear walls. For example, at shear wall on grids Bx in West building (WP457D in RISA model), the HD5 holdown is shown at approximately 6'-3" from the west end of the SW-2 shear wall. Analysis programs typically calculate holdown and shear wall demands based on the overall length of the shear wall, so when the holdown is not at the ends of the shear wall, the holdown and shear wall demands will exceed values calculated by the analysis program.      B. Some shear walls are substantially longer in analysis model than in plan set, such as WP910B (grid 2 between CW and FW in West building), WP457A (grid 4x between grids Cw and Fw in West building), or don't consider openings that interrupt them, such as WP475A (grid 2 between grids Kx and Mw in West building).      C. Some shear walls are substantially shorter in analysis model than in plan set, such as WP469F (grid 3 near grid Cx in the West building), which may cause calculations to result in a lower demand in these shear walls and holdowns than if these walls were modeled with their actual length.Structural Engineer (3)

Comment: Sheet A304. The covered area at Level 3 that is on the east side of Unit A is quite large (approx. 6'x20') is this space intended to be a roof deck? If so, show how the space will be accessed from the dwelling unit(s).

Subject: 01 Administration
Comment: Sheet A305. SBC 106.5.4, 706.5.2- Plans show wood framed canopies but do not appear to provide notes or details showing how they will be constructed.  Revise the plans to clarify this construction and clarify if they will include concealed space or not.  NOTE: It is assumed they will not include concealed space (ie. rafters will be exposed below; no soffit) for SBC 706.5.2 Exception 1.

Subject: 03 Use and Occupancy
Comment: Sheet G000. Revise the occupancy classifications for the following: 1. SBC 311- General storage rooms/spaces are typically classified as S-1 (any material) because S-2 is limited to noncombustible materials. If S-2 is the appropriate classification for this project, provide notes to clarify only noncombustible materials/items may be stored in those spaces. 2. SBC 406.3.1- Private garages that are less than 1,000sf floor area may be classified as U-garage. Use this classification (in lieu of S-2) to use the SBC 1106.5 accessible van vertical height exception.     EGRESS COM

Subject: 07 Fire Resistive Assemblies
Comment: Sheet A121. SBC 706.6 and/or 706.6.1- Revise the plans to show vertical continuity compliance for the portion of fire wall located between the exterior exit stair and Unit A.

Subject: 10 Means of Egress
Comment: Sheets A100. SBC 106.5.4- Revise the Site Plan to indicate the space on the west side of this property is a public right-of-way or private property, similar to the notation for the 16' alley on the south side of the property.

Subject: 10 Means of Egress
Comment: Sheet A121. SBC 1027.6- Revise the plans to show minimum 1hr fire barrier construction between the garage and the exterior exit stair.

Subject: 10 Means of Egress
Comment: Sheet A121. SBC 1109.1- Accessible spaces are required to be provide with not less than one accessible means of egress (AMOE).  Revise the plans to show an AMOE for Unit C and Unit D. Common AMOE options are stairs (1009.3) or elevators (1009.4).

Subject: 10 Means of Egress
Comment: Sheet A301. SBC 1011.7.4- There shall not be enclosed usable space under the exterior exit stair unless it is completely enclosed with 1hr rated construction. Revise the plans to provide compliant notes, as it is unclear if this stair is enclosed or not.

Subject: 10 Means of Egress
Comment: Sheet A301. SBC 1010.1.9- Revise the plans (ie. Door Schedule) to provide hardware notes for the exterior gates on the NW and NE corners of the property to indicate they will be readily openable on the egress side.

Subject: 11 Accessibility
Comment: Sheet A121. SBC 1107.6.3- Revise the plans to indicate Units C and D are required to comply as accessible Type B units. For example, see SBC Chapter 11 and ICC A117.1-2009 for the following: 1. Bathroom grab bar reinforcement- see ICC A117.1-2009 Section 1004.11. Applies to at least one bathroom in Unit C and D. 2. Elevator- see ICC A117.1-2009 for sections 407.3.6, Table 407.4.1, and 1004.7. 3. Kitchen- see ICC A117.1-2009 Section 1004.12. 4. Laundry- see ICC A117.1-2009 Section 1004.10. 5. Threshold at sliding door (Level 3 of Unit D)- see ICC A117.1-2009 Sections 404.2.3.3 and 404.2.4.

Subject: 11 Accessibility
Comment: Sheet A301. SBC 406.2.3, 1106.2 item 1, 1106.5- Where accessible dwelling units are provided, and parking is also provided, accessible parking is required. Revise the plans to show at least one accessible van parking stall with access aisle is provided in the garage. Per ICC A117.1-2009 Sections 502.2 & 502.4- dimensions for accessible van parking space and access aisle can either be: 132" wide parking space w/60" wide access aisle; or 96" wide parking space w/96" wide access aisle. ICC A117.1-2009 Section 502.6- requires a 98" vertical height clearance; however, SBC 1106.5 Exception allows 7' vertical height clearance for U-garages that serve R-3 occupancies. X

Subject: Zoning - SMC 23.45 - Multifamily
Comment: Design Standards. Per SMC 23.45.529.H.1, Building entry orientation standards for apartments. For each apartment structure, a principal shared pedestrian entrance is required that faces either a street or a common amenity area, such as a landscaped courtyard, that abuts and has direct access to the street. Subject: Zoning - SMC 23.54 - Parking, Access, and Solid Waste
Comment: Bike Parking Location and Access. Per SMC 23.54.015.K.2, a). Provide secure locations and arrangements of long-term bicycle parking, with features such as locked rooms or cages and bicycle lockers. The bicycle parking should be installed in a manner that avoids creating conflicts with automobile accesses and driveways. b). For a garage with bicycle parking and motor vehicle parking for more than two dwelling units, provide pedestrian and bicycle access to long-term bicycle parking that is separate from other vehicular entry and egress points or uses the same entry or egress point but has a marked walkway for pedestrians and bicyclists. c).Provide adequate lighting in the bicycle parking area and access routes to it.d.If short-term bicycle parking facilities are not clearly visible from the street or sidewalk or adjacent on-street bicycle facilities, install directional signage in adequate amounts and in highly visible locations in a manner that promotes easy way finding for bicyclists. e).Provide signage to long-term bicycle parking that is oriented to building users. f).Long-term bicycle parking shall be located where bicyclists are not required to carry bicycles on exterior stairs with more than five steps to access the parking. The Director, as a Type I decision, may allow long-term bicycle parking for rowhouse and townhouse development to be accessed by stairs with more than five steps, if the slope of the lot makes access with five or fewer steps infeasible. g).Where practicable, long-term bicycle parking shall include a variety of rack types to accommodate different types of bicycles. h).Install bicycle parking hardware so that it can perform to its manufacturer's specifications and any design criteria promulgated by the Director of the Seattle Department of Transportation, allowing adequate clearance for bicycles and their riders. Please revise and update the plan set as needed

Comment: Air Leakage Building Test/ G1.21: The completed building shall be tested and the air leakage rate of the building envelope shall not exceed 0.25 cfm/ft² at a pressure differential of 0.3 inches water gauge at the upper 95 percent confidence interval in accordance with ASTM E 779 per SEC C402.5.1.2.  A report that includes the tested surface area, floor area, air by volume, stories above grade, and leakage rates shall be submitted to the building owner and the code official.  If the tested rate exceeds that defined here by up to 0.15 cfm/ft², a visual inspection of the air barrier shall be conducted and any leaks noted shall be sealed to the extent practicable.  An additional report identifying the corrective actions taken to seal air leaks shall be submitted to the building owner and the Code Official and any further requirement to meet the leakage air rate will be waived.  If the tested rate exceeds 0.40 cfm/ft², corrective actions must be made and the test completed again.  A test above 0.40 cfm/ft² will not be accepted.  These requirements shall be indicated on the drawing.  The construction documents shall also contain a diagram showing the building's pressure boundary in plans and sections and a calculation of the area of the pressure boundary to be considered in the test per SEC C402.5.1.1 #5.

Comment: Air Leakage Building Test/ G1.21: The completed building shall be tested and the air leakage rate of the building envelope shall not exceed 0.25 cfm/ft² at a pressure differential of 0.3 inches water gauge at the upper 95 percent confidence interval in accordance with ASTM E 779 per SEC C402.5.1.2.  A report that includes the tested surface area, floor area, air by volume, stories above grade, and leakage rates shall be submitted to the building owner and the code official.  If the tested rate exceeds that defined here by up to 0.15 cfm/ft², a visual inspection of the air barrier shall be conducted and any leaks noted shall be sealed to the extent practicable.  An additional report identifying the corrective actions taken to seal air leaks shall be submitted to the building owner and the Code Official and any further requirement to meet the leakage air rate will be waived.  If the tested rate exceeds 0.40 cfm/ft², corrective actions must be made and the test completed again.  A test above 0.40 cfm/ft² will not be accepted.  These requirements shall be indicated on the drawing.  The construction documents shall also contain a diagram showing the building's pressure boundary in plans and sections and a calculation of the area of the pressure boundary to be considered in the test per SEC C402.5.1.1 #5. Cycle 2:  The area of the pressure boundary shall be calculated for the air leakage building test in lieu of the floor area as shown on drawing G1.21.Energy (8)

Subject: Drainage Review Required - No OSM (<1,500 sf NPRHS)
Comment: A quick measurement within the site plan showed that the new plus replaced hard surface areas (including the DADU, roof overhang and the portion of the covered porch) is 830 square feet approximately. Drainage Review is required for this project per the 2021 Seattle Stormwater  Manual Volume 1, Chapter 8, since there is 750 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface and/or 5,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity. Stormwater Code/Manual requirements are based on the amount of new and replaced hard surface associated with the project. Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas, driveways, walkways, and parking areas. Permeable pavement and pavers are considered a hard surface. Please complete and submit the following documents: 1) Standard Construction Stormwater Control and Soil Amendment  (CSC/SOIL) Plan 2) Standard Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan 3) On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (Note: Because the proposed amount of new and replaced hard surface is more than 750 square feet, but less than 1500 square feet, only the "Project Information" and "Site Information" section of the Project Summary tab in the OSM Calculator must be completed.  Import Project Summary (a.k.a. Site and Drainage Control Summary Sheet) sh from the OSM Calculator into the DWC Plan.) Please enter the following information in the "Site Information" section of the Site and Drainage Control Summary Sheet: a) The "Approved Point of Stormwater Discharge" is "On Site Infiltration (No Off-Site Point of Discharge)". b) The "Drainage Basin" is "N/A" for Single Family Projects. c) The "Approved Point of Wastewater Discharge" is "Public Sanitary Sewer Main". d) The "Approved Point of Subsurface Discharge" is "On Site Infiltration". The Seattle Stormwater Manual and all of the templates and documents mentioned above are available at http://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code. The CSC/SOIL Plan and DWC Plan must be combined with the submitted Plan Set PDF.Drainage (4)

Subject: DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F.
Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2.1. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer, as the project is located within the setbacks of a steep slope. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The infiltration testing shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.

Subject: Slope Stability Analysis for Infiltration in Steep Slope or Landslide Prone Area Setback.
Comment: The proposed infiltration facility appears to be within the setback above an ECA Steep Slope or Landslide Prone Area where infiltration is limited. Per Vol. 3, Section 3.2, Site Constraints, infiltration is limited within the slope or within a setback of 10 times the height of the slope to a maximum of 500 feet above the top of the slope.  Infiltration within this area may be feasible provided that a detailed slope stability analysis is completed by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer. Please submit a detailed slope stability analysis prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer and reference the analysis and distance from the ECA Steep Slope and/or Landslide Prone Area in the Drainage Report.

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped steep slope and potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers.       Revegetation requirements apply within steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been addressed. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.    1. Provide an existing conditions plan. Clearly show the steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs and their buffers on the existing conditions plan.     Public facing GIS mapping tool, helpful for viewing property and generating a site plan with required information: ArcGIS Web Application    2. Provide a brief description/identification of the existing ground coverage within the area of temporary and permanent disturbance in the ECA. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping (vegetation species), blackberry or other invasive species, tree species, patio, pathway, driveway, stairway, etc. Calculate the area in square footage and show this on the existing conditions plan.     3. Show locations of all existing trees located within and adjacent to the disturbance area consistently across all plan sheets. Include a tree table with genus, species, common name, DSH (diameter at standard height), dripline diameter and if trees/vegetation are proposed to remain or be removed. Please number trees consistently within table and across all plan sheets.    4. Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list of the existing ecological functions performed by the trees and vegetation within the steep slope and potential landslide prone ECA. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration (SMC 25.09.065.C.2.a). ECA Revegetation (4)

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: [25.09.065.B]  SHEET: ECA code section SMC 25.09.065 requires that you avoid or minimize tree and vegetation removal within steep slope ECAs. For existing trees proposed for removal SDCI requires that you demonstrate the use of required mitigation sequencing in the project development phase (SMC 25.09.065.B.1). These required steps are meant to find the least environmentally-damaging practicable alternative to achieve a project need to construct the updates you are proposing and trees you are proposing for removal.  1. Include items a. through f. in a table with responses to each. Additionally, show how you have considered these items in order per SMC 25.09.065.B2. which states that the lower priority measures (b. through f.) shall only be applied if the higher priority measure (a.) is infeasible or inapplicable. Mitigation sequencing must be undertaken in the order of priority listed.     a. Avoiding the impact altogether by not taking a certain action or parts of an action;  b. Minimizing impacts by limiting the degree or magnitude of the action and its implementation by using appropriate technology, best management practices, and/or by taking affirmative steps to avoid or reduce impacts;  c. Rectifying the impact by repairing, rehabilitating, or restoring the affected environment;  d. Reducing or eliminating the impact over time by preservation and maintenance operations;  e. Compensating for the impact by replacing, enhancing, or providing substitute resources or environments; and  f. Monitoring the impact and the compensation projects undertaken under subsection 25.09.065.B.1.e and taking appropriate corrective measures.

Subject: Adjustments
Comment: Adjustment Clarification:  Thank you for providing additional depth to the entry canopy as suggested in the SDR guidance.  The canopy's depth appears to be inconsistently represented in this plan set —review and revise for consistency and show the canopy on the plot plan.  The maximum depth (1.5' from the property line) is encouraged and supported.   Please add a design guideline-based rationale to your request in the next review cycle.

Subject: General Design Review Comment
Comment: Window Treatments:  Thank you for providing details clarifying the metal trim window treatments.  While this treatment is an acceptable trim method where windows are surrounded by fiber cement panel systems, this treatment falls short in the brick volumes, where punched openings would be more contextually responsive (per the SDR guidance and per context precedents provided in your packet) and where such treatment would lend "realism" to the brick cladding.  It is noted that simply insetting the windows within the existing openings would be sufficient, providing much more shadow detail than proposed with a 2" trim.  Another option would be to extend the metal trim further beyond the facade to enhance the shadow effects thereof (DC2-D-1, DC2-D-2, Central Area Supplemental Guideline CS3-1-a). Please also clarify your renderings which appear to show a 3" trim.

Subject: General Design Review Comment
Comment: Street Activation & Entries:  It is understood that the building is "stepping down" in response to the on-site topography.  However, in reviewing these construction plans, it would appear that the building is lowered beyond this point to achieve a height bonus and FAR exemption related to the basement level.  While this is acceptable, the main entry on 15th Ave should not suffer from this strategy.  Graphically study methods to provide direct access from the sidewalk to the building, without a ramp requiring a circuitous route to the building.  Consider widening the path leading to the structure to provide enhanced opportunities for interaction, more comfortable passage of residents and visitors in both directions simultaneously, and to make the entry more legible.  Another option would be to add steps directly from the sidewalk to the entry, in addition to the ramp, possibly in conjunction with a deeper recess at the entry to provide the necessary space (CS1-C-1, CS1-C-2, PL3-A-1, PL3-A-1-c, Central Area Supplemental Guidelines PL3-1-g, PL3-2-i, PL3-2-j).

Subject: General Design Review Comment
Comment: Entry Sequence:  Consider providing character landscaping around the main entry to the building to provide better legibility for pedestrians and better privacy for residents.  With only one main entry, that entry should be made special through attention to detail.  Character landscaping should include plant species repeated in the amenity area at the interior of the site for design cohesion.

Subject: General Design Review Comment
Comment: Materials:  The Central Area Supplemental Guidelines call for vibrant, bold use of color and there are contextual cues in the immediate vicinity that underscore this.  Graphically study an alternative color for the composite wood accent material that provides better contrast with the brick volumes on all four facades of the building.  Matching the red cedar soffit would be an acceptable approach, although you are encouraged to explore ways to be even more playful and contextually responsive as you consider this correction (Central Area Supplemental Guidelines DC4-2-a, A.1-1-b, c, d).

Note, Design Review staff have noted problems with panels 5/16" or less in thickness.  These panels are more prone to deformation and are less forgiving when applied to rough framing, which may lead to delays after the first Land Use inspection if the building's appearance does not match the approved drawings. Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: Revegetation requirements apply within ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within ECAs: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set. A. A1.0 Existing landscape/site plan: Provide EXISTING ground coverage conditions. ECA code section SMC 25.09.065 requires that you avoid or minimize tree and vegetation removal within ECAs.  -  Provide total area of impact that requires mitigation: a. Total new hard surface area; b. Total temporary construction disturbance area  c. Use this calculation (a+b=c) for total area of impact that requires mitigation. - Provide a brief description of the EXISTING ground coverage within these areas. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping, blackberry or other invasive species, trees, patio, pathway.  - Show locations of all existing trees within the ECAs and their buffers to be removed and/or retained. Include a tree table with tree genus, species, common name, DBH (diameter at breast height), driplines and health. Update to show correct tree dripline diameter measurements (inner and outer root zones) as they appear to be incorrect as noted in arborist report. - Clearly delineate the "Steep Slopes (ECA1)"  and "Potential slide (ECA2)" in the plan set. The SDCI External GIS Map is a helpful tool to locate designated ECAs. https://seattlecitygis.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=f822b2c6498c4163b0cf 908e2241e9c2 - Include a brief summary of the existing ecological functions performed by the ECA on and adjacent to the site. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration. B. A1.0 Proposed landscape plan/table: Based on existing ground coverage, please show/delineate the PROPOSED mitigation in the form of replanting. Please update site plan and provide the information below: - The location, size, species, quantities and spacing of trees/shrubs to be newly planted per calculation on ECA standard mitigation plan. Tree replacement can be 1:1, shrub multiplier is 0.042 times total area that requires mitigation (see cor. B). https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Forms/TreeVegetationStandardMitigation Plan.pdf - New trees must be two gallon size (4-6' height) and shrubs one gallon.  - Planting selections shall be straight NATIVE species suited to specific site conditions/orientation, no cultivars or hybrids are allowed. - Add a note that areas that have been cleared, graded, or compacted are to be amended with organic matter prior to planting. Use finely shredded mulch, minimum 4 ” depth between new plantings. - Clearly delineate the "Steep Slopes (ECA1)"  and "Potential slide (ECA2)" in the plan set. The SDCI External GIS Map is a helpful tool to locate designated ECAs. https://seattlecitygis.maps.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=f822b2c6498c4163b0cf 908e2241e9c2 C. A1.0 Proposed landscape plan/table: For existing trees proposed for removal SDCI requires that you demonstrate the use of required mitigation sequencing in the project development phase (SMC 25.09.065.B.1). These required steps are meant to find the least environmentally-damaging practicable alternative to achieve a project need to construct the updates you are proposing and trees you are proposing for removal.  Include items a. through f.in a table with responses to each. Additionally, show how you have considered of these items in order per SMC 25.09.065.B2. which states that the lower priority measures (b. through f.) shall only be applied if the higher priority measure (a.) is infeasible or inapplicable. Mitigation sequencing must be undertaken in the order of priority listed.    a. Avoiding the impact altogether by not taking a certain action or parts of an action; b. Minimizing impacts by limiting the degree or magnitude of the action and its implementation by using appropriate technology, best management practices, and/or by taking affirmative steps to avoid or reduce impacts; c. Rectifying the impact by repairing, rehabilitating, or restoring the affected environment; d. Reducing or eliminating the impact over time by preservation and maintenance operations; e. Compensating for the impact by replacing, enhancing, or providing substitute resources or environments; and f. Monitoring the impact and the compensation projects undertaken under subsection 25.09.065.B.1.e and taking appropriate corrective measures. D. A1.0 Proposed landscape plan: Add the following standard notes. - The following monitoring and maintenance is required for a period of 5 years from date of plant installation. Self-monitoring is sufficient. No documentation is required to be submitted to SDCI unless requested. - 80 percent survival of new trees and vegetation planted at the end of five years; - Annual inspections of the plants; - Replacement of failed plants; - Removal of exotic invasive species that have become established;  - Photographic documentation of planting success retained for the five-year period; and - No permanent irrigation is allowed on erosion hazard areas or their buffers. E. A1.0 and CSC Site plans: Provide a highly visible and durable protective barrier during construction to prevent access and to protect environmentally critical areas where applicable. Show tree/veg protection fencing at driplines as much as possible. Include dimensions between tree trunks and tree protection fences so workers and inspectors can accurately site them in the field. Tree & Vegetation detail here, use symbol (-o-o-o-): https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/TreeDetail.pdfRevegetation (1)

Subject: Category 1 Peat Settlement ECA – Infiltration/Dispersion Required for New Hard Surfaces
Comment: This site is in a Category 1 Peat Settlement ECA.  Per subsection E of SMC Section 25.09.110, development in a Category I peat settlement-prone area shall not increase the total hard surface on the site unless the Director approves using an infiltration facility, dispersion facility or soil amendments that offset the lost infiltration function. New hard surfaces or replaced hard surfaces that are not currently connected to an offsite drainage system will not be permitted to connect to an offsite drainage system.  Please submit a Drainage Report with calculations demonstrate no lost infiltration function.  One option is to use the requirements for projects with No Off-site Point of Discharge in Volume 3, Section 4.3.2 of the Seattle Stormwater Manual.  See also Director's Rule 14-2008 - Infiltration Facilities in Peat Settlement-Prone Areas.Drainage (5)

Comment: Revegetation requirements apply within ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. ECA code section SMC 25.09.065 requires that you avoid or minimize tree and vegetation removal within ECAs: a. Total new hard surface area; b. Total temporary construction disturbance area  c. Use this calculation (a+b=c) for total area of impact that requires mitigation. - Provide a brief description of the EXISTING ground coverage within these areas. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping, blackberry or other invasive species, trees, patio, pathway.  - Show locations of all existing trees within the ECAs and their buffers to be removed and/or retained. Include a tree table with tree genus, species, common name, DBH (diameter at breast height), driplines and health. - Include a brief summary of the existing ecological functions performed by the ECA on and adjacent to the site. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration. D. D. L-1.0: Based on existing ground coverage, please show/delineate the PROPOSED mitigation in the form of replanting on a PROPOSED landscape/site plan and table. Please update site plan to show the entire lot and provide the information below: - The location, size, species, quantities and spacing of trees/shrubs to be newly planted per calculation on ECA standard mitigation plan. Use finely shredded mulch, minimum 4 ” depth between new plantings. E.  For existing trees proposed for removal SDCI requires that you demonstrate the use of required mitigation sequencing in the project development phase (SMC 25.09.065.B.1). These required steps are meant to find the least environmentally-damaging practicable alternative to achieve a project need to construct the updates you are proposing and trees you are proposing for removal.  Include items a. through f.in a table with responses to each. Additionally, show how you have considered of these items in order per SMC 25.09.065.B2. which states that the lower priority measures (b. through f.) shall only be applied if the higher priority measure (a.) is infeasible or inapplicable. Mitigation sequencing must be undertaken in the order of priority listed.    a. Avoiding the impact altogether by not taking a certain action or parts of an action; b. Minimizing impacts by limiting the degree or magnitude of the action and its implementation by using appropriate technology, best management practices, and/or by taking affirmative steps to avoid or reduce impacts; c. Rectifying the impact by repairing, rehabilitating, or restoring the affected environment; d. Reducing or eliminating the impact over time by preservation and maintenance operations; e. Compensating for the impact by replacing, enhancing, or providing substitute resources or environments; and f. Monitoring the impact and the compensation projects undertaken under subsection 25.09.065.B.1.e and taking appropriate corrective measures. F. Minimizing impacts by limiting the degree or magnitude of the action and its implementation by using appropriate technology, best management practices, and/or by taking affirmative steps to avoid or reduce impacts; c. Rectifying the impact by repairing, rehabilitating, or restoring the affected environment; d. Reducing or eliminating the impact over time by preservation and maintenance operations; e. Subject: Zoning - General and Special Corrections
Comment: The AADU and DADU garage are shown to accommodate a two-wheeled vehicle through a runnel. While a runnel may alleviate minor obstructions, it is not clear how a two-wheel vehicle can be pushed up 8 steps, at right angles with 70-85% slopes, and also fit within the area dedicated for the runnel. Subject: Performance monitoring notes
Comment: SMC 22.170.110 A. Please modify the shoring monitoring notes to reflect the following monitoring requirements:   *Monitoring points established along the curbline and centerline of adjacent roadways need to be monitored when total wall movements reach 0.5 inch or at SDOT request.   *Indicate on the plan the minimum monitoring point spacing along the top of the wall and minimum distance behind the wall that reflect the recommendations provided by the geotechnical engineer.   *Establish a baseline reading of monitoring points on the ground surface and settlement-sensitive structures behind the shoring wall alignment prior to dewatering, excavation, and installation of the shoring systems.   *A licensed surveyor (not the contractor) must do the surveying at least once a week.   *Survey frequency can be decreased after the shoring system has been installed and excavation is complete if the data indicates little or no additional movement. Surveying must continue until the permanent structure (including floor slabs as braces) is complete up to final and street grades. The survey frequency will be determined by the geotechnical engineer after review and approval by SDCI and SDOT.   *The geotechnical engineer shall review survey data and provide an evaluation of wall performance along with survey data to SDCI and SDOT on at least a weekly basis. Immediately and directly, notify SDCI and SDOT if any unusual or significantly increased movement occurs.   *Immediately and directly notify the geotechnical and structural engineers, wall designer, SDCI, and SDOT if 0.5 inches of movement occurs between two consecutive readings and when total movements reach 0.5 inch. At that amount of movement, the engineers and designers shall determine the cause of displacement and develop remedial measures sufficient to limit total wall movements to 1 inch. All earthwork and construction activities must be directed towards immediate implementation of remedial measures necessary to limit total wall movements to what has been defined as acceptable by the design team and SDOT and SDCI (as indicated above). These notes are required because of the height of the ultrablock temporary shoring and it's proximity to the ROW and are a condition of the shoring type being accepted. The geotechnical engineer must determine when the monitoring shall start based on their recommendations and the construction sequencing.  Sheet A1.02ECA GeoTech (1) 04 06

Subject: 16 Lateral Design
Comment: BRIDGE CONNECTION See plan sheet S2.1& S2.2: ASCE 7-16 Section 12.1.3  Continuous Load Path and Interconnection. A continuous load path, or paths, with adequate strength and stiffness shall be provided to transfer all forces from the point of application to the ﬁnal point of resistance.  All parts of the  structure between separation joints shall be interconnected to  form a continuous path to the seismic force-resisting system, and the connections shall be capable of transmitting the seismic force (Fp) induced by the parts being connected.  Any smaller portion Of the structure shall be tied to the remainder of the structure with elements that have a design strength capable of transmitting a seismic force of 0.133 times the short-period design spectral response acceleration parameter, SDS, times the weight of the smaller portion or 5% of the portion ’s weight, whichever is greater.  This connection force does not apply to the overall design of the seismic force-resisting system.  Connection design forces need not exceed the maximum forces that the structural system can deliver to the connection. ASCE 7-10 12.12. requires  accounting for relative displacements of the buildings. --Show how the bridge design accounts for the potential of the two buildings to seismically move out-of-phase from each other in both orthogonal directions.  (Typically results in a seismic joint being provided.) --Add collector-distributors as required to dissipate force in the diaphragm as required. --Provide details at the interface of the bridge and the building structures on either side. Provide detail cuts on the plans. (Date: 12/16/2022)

Subject: General Design Review Comment
Comment: Design ReviewIn the Design Review documents submitted for this project, the exterior cladding materials have been represented as flat, plumb, square and true. In those drawings the material joints are aligned, of uniform dimension and appearance, metal flashings are unbent, and the panels show no bowing, buckling, warping or other deformation. Because thin cementitious materials have little inherent structural integrity, this appearance is dependent on a high-quality installation on a uniformly flat and stable substrate and complete details demonstrating this are required. Those details should include; typical wall assembly, material transitions, corner details (inside and out), typical window and door (head/jamb/sill), type and spacing of furring material, flashing type and gauge, treatment of field-cut edges, siding flatness tolerance (an industry standard is <1/8" over 10'-0"), and dimensioned panel layout (can be partial if global notes included to ensure panel alignment with openings and preclude cutting ‘inside corners ’ in panels). (SDR Comment 3.b)

Subject: General Tree Comment
Comment: On Thursday April 6th I performed a site visit to confirm tree measurements and take a look at tree conditions. my measurements for the south tree:  approximately 60- inch Diameter at standard height (it was not possible to accurately measure diameter due to the obstructions of the fence and garage) this south tree has drip line extents from the center of the trunk of 20 feet. This tree is growing against the existing garage with an approximately 2 foot overgrowth of the trunk over the structure and there are some signs of decay between the root flares of the lower trunk. The North tree is approximately 72 inches in Diameter ( again it was not possible to access the full trunk to make an accurate diameter measurement, This tree has a drip line from trunk center of 24 feet, there was thick English ivy engulfing the base, to perform a basic visual assessment this ivy should be removed. Both trees are mature and if retained should be protected to the drip line at a minimum, any incursion into the drip line of the trees is likely to create a high risk in the near future. At initial correction request I requested a report per the requirements of 25.11.050 D1-5:  D.The Director may require a tree protection report by a registered tree service provider who provides the following information: 1.Tree evaluation with respect to its general health, damage, danger of falling, proximity to existing or proposed structures, and/or utility services; 2.Evaluation of the anticipated effects of proposed construction on the viability of the tree; 3.A hazardous tree assessment, if applicable; 4.Plans for supervising and/or monitoring implementation of any required tree protection or replacement measures; and 5.Plans for conducting post-construction site inspection and evaluation. As shown the site configuration that as it relates to the trees cannot be approved, I recommend a thorough evaluation of the trees is performed that can be used to inform the plan for the site and trees.Paul Humphries (1)

Subject: 16 Lateral Design
Comment: BRIDGE CONNECTION REPEAT CORRECTION: Please note: The correction was reviewed and confirmed that the smaller of the two buildings is used to determine the seismic force for the connection design. --In lieu of providing a connection with enough capacity to exceed the (high) demand force, a seismic joint can be designed and used.  --Also to clarify, the seismic demand force would need to include the total building area at and above the level on the bridge. {Date: 4/24/2023}. [Original Correction] BRIDGE CONNECTION See plan sheet S2.1& S2.2: ASCE 7-16 Section 12.1.3  Continuous Load Path and Interconnection. A continuous load path, or paths, with adequate strength and stiffness shall be provided to transfer all forces from the point of application to the ﬁnal point of resistance.  All parts of the  structure between separation joints shall be interconnected to  form a continuous path to the seismic force-resisting system, and the connections shall be capable of transmitting the seismic force (Fp) induced by the parts being connected.  Any smaller portion Of the structure shall be tied to the remainder of the structure with elements that have a design strength capable of transmitting a seismic force of 0.133 times the short-period design spectral response acceleration parameter, SDS, times the weight of the smaller portion or 5% of the portion ’s weight, whichever is greater.  This connection force does not apply to the overall design of the seismic force-resisting system.  Connection design forces need not exceed the maximum forces that the structural system can deliver to the connection. ASCE 7-10 12.12. requires  accounting for relative displacements of the buildings. --Show how the bridge design accounts for the potential of the two buildings to seismically move out-of-phase from each other in both orthogonal directions.  (Typically results in a seismic joint being provided.) --Add collector-distributors as required to dissipate force in the diaphragm as required. --Provide details at the interface of the bridge and the building structures on either side. Provide detail cuts on the plans. (Date: 12/16/2022) General Comm        al Comments

Subject: 18 Foundations & Retaining Walls
Comment: 1. UPLIFT AT FOUNDATIONS The holdowns appear to have significant tension demands, compared to the counteracting dead load.  For example: HDU5 holdowns along the eastern exterior wall are noted in calculations (pages L-3 and L-7) to have a holdown demand of approximately 4 kips. The holdowns are anchored to a small foundation wall/footing, which weighs as little as 0.26 kips/ft (assuming minimum overall height of 2'-2" noted in 4/S3.1), so 0.6D = 0.16 kips/ft. Framing is north-south for most levels, so there is very little tributary load to this wall from stories above. Consequently, it appears that a tributary length of approximately 25 feet would be required to resist the uplift reaction (4 kips / 0.16 kips/ft = 25ft), which seems like a significant extent for a building of this size.  Provide calculations that demonstrate that the structure shown in plans has adequate dead load to counteract uplift forces due to seismic and wind lateral loads. Revise plans as appropriate.

Subject: PE Evaluation & Certification Required
Comment: [Sheet ___ ]  If you intend to reuse existing side sewer, an Evaluation and Certification of the existing side sewers by a Professional Engineer is necessary because the existing side sewer/s were installed prior to 2004.   SS Code 21.16.240 and the Requirements for Design and Construction of Side Sewers Director's Rule (DR 4-2011) detail the requirements for use of an existing side sewer. In summary, a civil engineer must evaluate and certify the existing side sewer; if the side sewer is 50 years or older, the side sewer will need to be lined; if the existing side sewer is less than 50 years old, the side sewer must either be lined or the Evaluation and Certification process must include a pressure test. Please add  a very clear, boxed note added to the Drainage and Wastewater Control Plan that  the existing side sewer must be Evaluated and Certified by a Professional Engineer and either rehabilitated (i.e. lined) or pressure tested all the way to the public mainline in the street.  The completed Evaluation and Certification form must be submitted to the inspector during construction.  The form is available with the following link: http://www.seattle.gov/dpd/permits/permittypes/sidesewer/default.htm

Depending on the information provided for review, additional correction cycles may result. Provide consistency across the plan set. A. Based on the drip line of existing trees and the proposed project, it does not appear that any excavation and/or construction-related activity will occur within the tree protection areas of any on- or off-site trees. SDCI's standard tree and vegetation protection is not required.    Please clearly note on ALL plan view sheets a defined "development impact area." The development impact area is the area on the site affected by proposed site improvements, site access, storage/stockpiling of materials, or construction activities such as grading, filling, trenching, or other excavation necessary to install utilities or access.    Include the following note on ALL plan view sheets: Tree Protection/Development Impact Area Requirements: (1) Retention and protection of all trees 6 inches or greater is required, unless approved for removal. (2) No tree removal or damage is authorized. (3) Excavation and ground disturbance is prohibited outside of the development impact area. (4) Construction-related activities, such as site access, heavy equipment use, storage, or stockpiling is prohibited outside of the development impact area unless located on existing hard surfaces.Tree (1)

Subject: No POD DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F.
Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2.1. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).  The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: Correction 1: General Information  This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs).     Revegetation requirements apply within mapped potential landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within mapped potential landslide prone ECAs: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements for mapped potential landslide prone ECAs have not been addressed. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.    ECA Revegetation (4)

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs).  Revegetation requirements apply within potential landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within potential landslide prone ECAs: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements for potential landslide prone ECAs have not been addressed. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.  1. Provide an existing conditions plan showing the potential landslide prone area ECA.  2. Provide a brief description/identification of the existing ground coverage (prior to work done without permits) within the area of temporary and permanent disturbance. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping (vegetation species), blackberry or other invasive species, tree species, patio, pathway, driveway, stairway, etc. Calculate the area in square footage and show this on the site plan/existing conditions plan.  3. Show locations of all existing trees located within and adjacent to the disturbance area. Include a tree table with genus, species, common name, DSH (diameter at standard height), dripline diameter and if trees/vegetation are proposed to remain or be removed. Please number trees consistently within a table and on the existing conditions plan.  4. Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list of the existing ecological functions performed by the trees and vegetation within the potential landslide prone ECA. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration (SMC 25.09.065.C.2.a).  5. Remove designation of trees located in ECAs with "Tier categories" in the plan set/tables and arborist report. The ECA Code (SMC 25.09) does not use tiers to categorize trees.ECA Revegetation (3)

Total temporary construction disturbance area including all construction-related activities including, but not limited to construction access, staging area, temporary excavation, and areas of tree/vegetation removal.  c. Total area of impact that requires mitigation in the form of replanting. > add if needed: Calculations should only include areas within property lines, as we cannot approve information on the adjacent property. 1. Please show the location, size, species, quantities, and spacing of trees/shrubs to be newly planted. Use the ECA standard mitigation plan as a guide only. Shrub quantities can be determined by using multiplier 0.042 times the total area of impact that requires mitigation. Tree replacement quantities can be 1:1 or alternatively use an adjusted tree multiplier of 0.01 as the ECA standard mitigation plan multiplier results in an excessive number of trees. The goal is to provide a layered canopy. https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Forms/TreeVegetationStandardMitigation Plan.pdf 2. Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list, an analysis of how the mitigation plan compensates for lost ecological functions within the ECA.  3. Add note stating: Planting selections shall be Pacific Northwest native species suited to specific site conditions/orientation, no cultivars or hybrids are allowed. 4. Add note stating: New trees must be 4-6 feet in height and shrubs one-gallon size. 5. Add note stating: Areas that have been cleared, graded, or compacted are to be amended with organic matter prior to planting. Use finely shredded mulch, minimum 4 ” depth between new plantings. 6. Add note stating: The following monitoring and maintenance is required for a period of 5 years from date of plant installation. Self-monitoring is sufficient. No documentation is required to be submitted to SDCI unless requested. a.  80 percent survival of new trees and vegetation planted at the end of five years; b.  Annual inspections of the plants; c.  Replacement of failed plants; d.  Removal of exotic invasive species that have become established; and e. Photographic documentation of planting success retained for the five-year period.

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: Correction 1: General Information  This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped **steep slope environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers.       Revegetation requirements apply within ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been *met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.    Correction 2: Existing Conditions Sheet   1. A0.1, C01, C02,C03: Provide an existing conditions plan. Clearly show the ** steep slope and ECAs and their buffers on the existing conditions plans (like on L1). 2. A01 and arborist report: Trees in ECA's are not categorized by Tier category. Remove references and instead include "ECA".  3. A0.0, A0.1, C01, C02, C03, L1, L2: The land use analysis on A0.0 shows parcel a frequent transit area which requires no parking stalls, but you have proposed 4 parking stalls which in turn requires removal of tree #2, a 33 inch Douglas Fir in a steep slope ECA. The required mitigation sequencing narrative has not been met as avoiding impact the ECA can be avoided by not installing parking stalls in that location [25.09.065.B1a. In addition, the lower priority measures b. through f. shall only be applied if the higher priority measures are infeasible or inapplicable [25.09.065.2]. Subject: Seismic Site Class justification
Comment: The uploaded geotechnical report assumed Site Class D to determine seismic coefficients. To categorize the site as Site Class D, please demonstrate one of the following criteria: a) Shear wave velocity for the top 100 ft is between 600 and 1,200 ft/s. b) SPT-N blow counts for the top 100 ft are between 15 and 50 per foot. c) Undrained shear strength for the top 100 ft is between 1,000 and 2,000 lb/ft². The subsurface explorations presented in the uploaded geotechnical report lack sufficient detail to determine the site class. As per Section 11.4.3 of ASCE 7-16, when soil properties are not known in sufficient detail to determine the site class, Site Class D is selected as the default site class, and the value of Fa shall not be less than 1.2.  Please revise the seismic design parameters in the geotechnical report and update the structural design calculations accordingly.ECA GeoTech (10)

Subject: DWC
Comment: Sheet C1.2: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal: 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. Note: in order to infiltrate or disperse runoff on-site, a steep slope stability analysis by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer is required to demonstrate that these facilities will not impact the slope stability or adjacent properties. If the requirements for Projects with No Off-site Point of Discharge cannot be met, then a Storm Main Extension from E Spring St in 29th Ave will be required.

Provide automatic sprinklers in both the existing and new dwelling units pursuant to SFC Appendix B105.1.  The systems may be designed and installed per NFPA 13D standards.  The fire hydrant flow test noted above is not required. Revise Sheet A002 to indicate that a NFPA 13D fire sprinkler system will be installed in each dwelling unit. Subject: 01 Administration
Comment: Informational for applicant on how to respond to BB comments: FOR INFORMATION ONLY. NO RESPONSE REQUIRED In January 2022, SDCI transitioned to providing plan reviews via plan mark-up instead of traditional letters. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we rolled out the technology new to both applicants and SDCI staff. The primary change that we are asking of applicants is that they document responses to comments directly in the plan set provided to them by SDCI at the end of each review cycle instead of sending letters corresponding to each correction letter. When all responses are documented, we ask that applicants upload the response plan set (as document type Correction Response Plan Set or Correction Response Plan Set – Land Use) along with the new, clean plan set as (document type Plan Set or Plan Set – Land Use) for the next review cycle. We have a video to help you learn how to navigate the new process here:  https://youtu.be/KB8laufkd7M. As we transition to delivering marked up plan sets, you may receive both letters and marked up plan sets with our corrections documented. As a rule, please respond to any letter you receive with a letter and any marked-up plan set by embedding your responses in the marked-up plan set. We recognize that this transition requires changes to how you respond to our correction reports. We firmly believe that the changes we are instituting will lead to a reduction in the number of review cycles required to issue a permit. Remember, you will still: %ª Receive email notifications that a review has been completed. %ª Find review summary reports by discipline in the Seattle Services Portal as they are completed. %ª Submit updated plan sets after all reviews have been completed. What will be new is: %ª When all reviews are completed, you will receive a marked-up plan set which contains the comments from ALL the review disciplines. %ª Instead of preparing responses to each individual correction letter as you do today, you will be asked to reply to the comments directly in the marked-up plan set using either Bluebeam (requires a license) or Adobe Acrobat Reader (free).. %ª If you work with sub-consultants, you will need to coordinate with them to include their comments in your response plan set. Lastly, please help us perform reviews more efficiently! As we have worked on this transition, many of our reviewers indicated that they rely on bookmarks to navigate the (sometimes lengthy) plan sets that we receive from applicants. One thing that would allow us to review more quickly is to have applicants include a good set of bookmarks in every plan set that is submitted. Please follow the requirements for submitting pdf documents, outlined in Tip 106, General Standards for Plans and Drawings, [https://www.seattle.gov/DPD/Publications/CAM/cam106.pdf] to include a good set of bookmarks in every plan set you submit. NOTE: VERIFY THAT BOOKMARKS ARE NOT BROKEN PRIOR TO RESUBMITTING PLAN SETS. Bookmark links can become broken when sheets are added or removed from the plan set.

Comment: General Information  This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped **steep slope and potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers.       Revegetation requirements apply within ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have NOT been met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set. Please include columns for tree identifier numbers and canopy diameters correctly shown on sheets noted.Revegetation (2)

Comment: Sheet A1: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.Drainage (3)

In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.Drainage (3)
