Subject: Grading season restriction notes
Comment: Please add the following notes to the Temporary Erosion/Sedimentation Control Plan. These notes and requirements are in lieu of establishing a formalized seasonal grading restriction on the project and constitute the customary requirements that would be instituted for a seasonal grading extension:   A site visit from the Geotechnical Special Inspector shall occur during each day of active grading and in the event of significant rainfall which might compromise stabilization measures between November 1 and March 31. The determination of what constitutes significant rainfall is subject to the discretion of the Geotechnical Special Inspector. However, as a minimum standard, the Geotechnical Special Inspector is required to conduct a site visit if more than one-half inch of precipitation occurs on any given day. Any recommendations required to maintain stability of excavations and proper functioning of the sediment/erosion control system provided by the Geotechnical Special Inspector and SDCI personnel shall be implemented immediately. The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide copies of field reports to SDCI Site Development Services Section no later than 48 hours after each inspection. The field reports may be emailed to sdcigeo@seattle.gov. The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide written notice that the site has been stabilized following completion of grading.

Subject: DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F.
Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface. Comment: Repeated and revised item. SMC 22.170.110 A. Shoring system design calculations: The correction response memorandum from SSF, dated January 7, 2025, stated that the calculations for the shoring piles utilize ultimate passive pressure as an input in the Civil Tech program, with a separate safety factor of 1.2 applied. It seems there is some confusion between the safety factor and the ratio of ultimate to allowable design values. The soldier pile walls should use allowable passive pressure values, not ultimate or factored values. The results must demonstrate that the required safety factor is met using allowable passive pressure values of 175 pcf for the upper tier and 350 pcf for the lower tier. Revise the structural calculations accordingly.

Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload a PDF of the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Subject: Special Inspector nomination
Comment: SMC 22.170.130. Geotechnical Special Inspections is required for the proposed development. Please find SDCI Geotechnical Special Inspections Schedule form uploaded to the portal. Please see the instructions below to complete this form. 1) The form must be signed by the owner or owner's representative; the form cannot be signed by the contractor nor the geotechnical engineer.      2) The Inspection Agency must be the same engineer/firm that prepared the geotechnical report. 3) If the owner nominates a different engineer/firm to act as the Geotechnical Special Inspector, the new engineer must review the original geotechnical report and submit a letter indicating a review was performed, along with a statement of agreement with the evaluation and provisions contained in the report. If the new engineer does not agree with aspects of the report, rebuttal evaluations and recommendations must be included in the review letter. The plans must be revised accordingly and submitted to SDCI for review. Requests for changes of Special Inspection Agency that occur during plan review should be submitted with corrected plans. If the request occurs after permit issuance, send the required documents to the geotechnical reviewer.

Comment: Footing drains do not appear to be required and/or proposed.  If they are not, on the DWC Plan – sheet C1.1, please remove DWC Plan Note #1D that says, “ROOF DRAIN LINES. TO BE KEPT SPEARATE FROM FOOTING DRAINS AT ALL TIMES WHEN PRESENT. ”   However, if footing drains are proposed/required then on the DWC Plan – sheet C1.1, please clearly show and label the perimeter foundation/footing drain discharge lines ( “FD” or “DRN ”) being routed directly to and passing through a catch basin prior to connecting to the onsite sanitary sewer connection to the combined sewer main. Footing drains, when applicable, must be routed separately from the downspouts and directly to an onsite catch basin prior to connecting to the approved point of subsurface discharge. Per the Side Sewer Director's Rule 4-2011, Section VII.C.5 “In no case shall downspouts be connected directly to a groundwater collection system or the tight line connection from a groundwater collection system. ” Please make sure to show and label a separate roof area storm drain collection system being routed to an onsite catch basin prior to connecting to the onsite sanitary sewer connection to the combined sewer main.   If footing drains are not proposed and/or required by another reviewer, please update DWC Plan Note #1D to instead say, “ROOF DRAIN LINES TO BE KEPT SEPARATE. Comment: General Drainage Review Information: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Subject: Shoring monitoring notes
Comment: SMC 22.170.110 A. Please provide the shoring monitoring notes on shoring plan to reflect the following SDCI minimum monitoring requirements:  1) Indicate on the plan the minimum monitoring point spacing along the top of the wall and minimum distance behind the wall that reflect the recommendations provided by the geotechnical engineer.  2) Establish a baseline reading of monitoring points on the ground surface and settlement-sensitive structures behind the shoring wall alignment prior to dewatering, excavation, and installation of the shoring systems.   3) A licensed surveyor (not the contractor) must do the surveying at least once a week.  4) Survey frequency can be decreased after the shoring system has been installed and excavation is complete if the data indicates little or no additional movement. Surveying must continue until the permanent structure (including floor slabs as braces) is complete up to final and street grades. The survey frequency will be determined by the geotechnical engineer after review and approval by SDCI and SDOT.  5) The geotechnical engineer shall review survey data and provide an evaluation of wall performance along with survey data to SDCI and SDOT on at least a weekly basis. Immediately and directly, notify SDCI and SDOT if any unusual or significantly increased movement occurs.  6) Immediately and directly notify the geotechnical and structural engineers, wall designer, SDCI, and SDOT if 0.5 inches of movement occurs between two consecutive readings and when total movements reach 0.5 inch. At that amount of movement, the engineers and designers shall determine the cause of displacement and develop remedial measures sufficient to limit total wall movements to 1 inch. All earthwork and construction activities must be directed towards immediate implementation of remedial measures necessary to limit total wall movements to what has been defined as acceptable by the design team and SDOT (as indicated above).

Subject: Seismic Site Class C
Comment: Repeated item. The correction response by JP Jones Engineering dated June 4, 2024 stated that "the lateral design was completed with seismic category D, which is conservative compared to category C. Therefore no revisions to the design necessary". This statement is incorrect. Seismic Category and Site Class are distinct classifications, and Site Class D is not always more conservative compared to Site Class C. For example, the site coefficient Fa is 1.2 for Ss >= 1.0, which is more conservative than the Fa for Site Class D. ASCE 7-16, Chapter 20. Based on subsurface information presented in boring 1, it appears that the average SPT blow count is greater than 50 within 100 feet of the ground surface, therefore the site class should be categorized as Site Class C. Please provide seismic design parameters for Site Class C and revise the structural design calculations accordingly.

The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped steep slope and potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been met. Show locations of all existing trees located within and adjacent to the disturbance area consistently across all plan sheets. The Seattle Stormwater Manual and all of the templates and documents mentioned above are available at http://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforc e-(a-z)/stormwater-code. Subject: Drainage Review Required - No OSM (<1,500 sf
Comment: Drainage Review is required for this project per the 2021 Seattle Stormwater  Manual Volume 1, Chapter 8, since there is 750 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface and/or 5,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity. Stormwater Code/Manual requirements are based on the amount of new and replaced hard surface associated with the project. Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas, driveways, walkways, and parking areas. Permeable pavement and pavers are considered a hard surface. Please complete and submit the following documents: 1) Standard Construction Stormwater Control and Soil Amendment  (CSC/SOIL) Plan 2) Standard Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan 3) On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (Note: If there is less than1500 square feet of new plus replaced hard surface area, OSM BMPs are not required and only the "Project Information" and "Site Information" section of the Project Summary tab in the OSM Calculator must be completed.   Add the Project Summary (a.k.a. Site and Drainage Control Summary Sheet) sheet from the OSM Calculator onto the DWC Plan. Please enter the following information in the "Site Information" section of the Site and Drainage Control Summary Sheet: a) The "Approved Point of Stormwater Discharge" is "Drainage Culvert" (in 1st Ave NE near intersection with N 130th St). b) The "Drainage Basin" is "N/A for Single Family Projects ". c) The "Approved Point of Wastewater Discharge" is "Public Sanitary Sewer" d) The "Approved Point of Subsurface Discharge" is "Drainage Culvert". The Seattle Stormwater Manual and all of the templates and documents mentioned above are available at http://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code. The CSC/SOIL Plan and DWC Plan must be combined with the submitted Plan Set PDF.Drainage (2)

For each relocated or required replacement tree, maintenance and monitoring is required for a five-year period. The period begins when the replacement tree is planted. Maintenance and monitoring shall include the following: 1.Sufficient maintenance actions to ensure survival of the replacement tree: a. Subject: Tree Replacement Requirements (SMC 25.11.090)
Comment: Your plan shows replacement of Tree 1, but removal of trees 1, 3,4,6, 8, and 9 must all meet tree replacement requirements. Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 trees removed in association with development must be replaced by one or more new trees designed to result, upon maturity, in a canopy cover that is at least roughly proportional to the canopy cover prior to tree removal. Replacement trees must also be native and/or culturally significant, and resilient to climate change (SMC 25.11.090.C.2). Please refer to Director ’s Rule 12-2023 for more information about tree replacement requirements. Please note that the GreenFactor Plant list referenced in this rule only lists bioretention trees, which are only appropriate in wet areas. Please choose a drought-tolerant species. Feel free to email me with species selection questions.Deborah McGarry (13)

Comment: SFR/AADU Connection: The proposed SFR/AADU connection does not meet the standards in DR 10-95. Document how the width of the connection meets the standards for a major connection. And see section 2 of DR 10-95, when an accessory use is required to be located in the principal structure (AADU), the portion of structure where the accessory use is located shall be physically connected by a building component which as usable interior living space on both sides. Subject: Scooter garage
Comment: Third request As proposed, this appears to be a partially below grade basement being labeled as "garage" in order to exempt it from DADU square footage allowances found in SMC 23.44.041. Table A, letter f. The intent of the code is not to permit the relabeling of an entire ~875 sq ft basement to garage in order to exempt the area unless it is a bona fide garage. Scooter garages are permitted by code and can include incidental utility functions such as water heaters and similar.  That said, the "garage" designation cannot be used in a indiscriminate manner to exempt out an entire floor in order for it to be within the allowances for a DADU. Subject: General
Comment: Air Leakage Testing: The maximum air leakage rate for any dwelling unit under any compliance path shall not exceed 4.0 air changes per hour.  Testing shall be conducted with a blower door at a pressure of 0.2 inches w.g per SEC R402.4.1.2.  This requirement shall be noted on the drawing.

Subject: General
Comment: ADU/ A2.0: a.  The heating and cooling for the accessory dwelling unit shall be controllable with a separate programmable thermostat in accordance with SEC R403.1.1 per SEC R501.1.2.  This requirement shall be noted on the drawing. b.  Local exhaust in compliance with SRC M1505 shall be provided for the ADU Kitchen.

Subject: General
Comment: Ventilation: a.  The whole-house ventilation system shall consist of one or more supply fans, one or more exhaust fans, or an ERV/ HRV with integral fans.  Each dwelling unit shall be equipped with local exhaust and whole house ventilation systems and shall comply with the SRC M1505.  The whole-house mechanical ventilation system shall provide outdoor air at a continuous rate as determined in accordance with the SRC Table M1505.4.3(1).  Either continuous or intermittent whole house exhaust fan shall be indicated on the drawing.  If intermittent whole house ventilation is intended, the ventilation rate factors per SRC Table M1505.4.3.2 shall be applied to the minimum ventilation requirement.  The run-time percentage in each 4-hour segment shall also be noted on the drawing for intermittent operated whole house ventilation.  b.  The minimum whole house ventilation rate shall be adjusted by the system coefficient in SRC Table M1505.4.3(2) based on the system type not meeting the definition of a balanced whole house ventilation system and/or not meeting the definition of a distributed whole house ventilation system per SRC M1505.4.3.1. c.  The airflow rates for each local exhaust fan and whole house exhaust fan shall be noted on the drawings (typical).

Subject: General
Comment: Exhaust Outlets: All environmental air exhaust outlets shall be a minimum of 3 ft. from operable openings into the building, 3 ft. from property lines, 10 ft. from mechanical air intakes per SRC M1504.3.  The exhaust outlets and the operable openings shall be shown on the elevation plans in compliance with SRC M1504.3 (typical).

Cycle 2: As SEC Table R406.3 Option 2.1 is selected, a heat recovery ventilation system with minimum sensible heat recovery efficiency of 0.65 is required.  If the required HRV is included with this construction permit, please refer to the Heat Recovery Ventilation (HRV) Detail on Plans Example in the attached link (https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/mechanical-code).  Alternatively, a Subject to Field Inspection (STFI) permit for the intended heat recovery system may be applied separately.  The design intent shall be indicated on the drawing.Energy (2)

Subject: General
Comment: Ventilation: The minimum whole house ventilation rate shall be adjusted by the system coefficient in SRC Table M1505.4.3(2) based on the system type not meeting the definition of a balanced whole house ventilation system and/or not meeting the definition of a distributed whole house ventilation system per SRC M1505.4.3.1. Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: It appears the site plan is showing proposed EV chargers in the required side yard. Per SMC 23.44.14.C.12, any heat pump or similar equipment shall not be located within 3 feet of any lot line. Update the plans to demonstrate compliance with SMC 23.44.014.C.12.

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential

Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including a completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Comment: On the DWC Plan, if applicable, please clearly show and label the perimeter foundation/footing drain discharge lines ( “FD” or “DRN ”) being routed directly to and passing through a catch basin prior to connecting to the onsite sanitary sewer connection to the combined sewer main. Catch basins for footing drains must have a 2 ’ deep minimum sump and a sump volume of 2 cubic feet.  This must be called out on the DWC Plan. Footing drains, when applicable, must be routed separately from the downspouts and directly to an onsite catch basin prior to connecting to the approved point of subsurface discharge. Per the Side Sewer Director's Rule 4-2011, Section VII.C.5 “In no case shall downspouts be connected directly to a groundwater collection system or the tight line connection from a groundwater collection system. ” Please show and label a separate roof area storm drain collection system being routed to an onsite catch basin prior to connecting to the onsite sanitary sewer connection to the combined sewer main. Comment: NEW & PARTIAL REPEAT CORRECTION On the DWC Plan, you are now showing the footing drains being routed to a non-infiltrating bioretention planter. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The provided lot coverage calculations appear to be incorrect. Per SMC 23.44.010.D.2, decks or parts of a deck that are 36 inches or less above existing grade as well as the first 36 inches of eaves and gutters that project from principal and accessory structures are exempt from lot coverage (i.e. most of section J on the DADU lot coverage diagram should be exempt area). Update the lot coverage diagrams to label and dimension all eaves and gutters for both the existing and proposed structures and clearly identify the first 36 ” of all eaves/gutter projections as exempt from lot coverage. Any eave/gutter projections in excess of 36 ” should be counted toward lot coverage. Additionally, it does not appear the existing steps that are above 36 ” from existing grade are being appropriately counted toward lot coverage. Update the lot coverage diagrams and calculations accordingly. Note, the outer most side of the posts that support the existing entry covering to the primary residence should be used to determine the wall plane. The eave/gutter projections less than 36" from the invisible wall line formed between the post supports are exempt from lot coverage per SMC 23.44.010.D.2.

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The elevations label maximum base height for the proposed DADU. However, parts of the DADU appear to exceed base height that are not otherwise a pitched, butterfly, or shed roof nor do they appear to meet any of the allowed projections in the footnotes of Table A for SMC 23.44.041. Base height is the point at which the vertical face of low side (west) of the structure meets the top of the sloped roof line. It appears that point on the plans is approximately 11" above max base height. Update the plans to clearly demonstrate that only the slope above vertical face of the structure exceeds max base height in accordance with Table for SMC 23.44.041 Letter k and Exhibit A for SMC 23.44.041.

Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Additionally, single-family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must also implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  On the Site Plan – sheet C-100, you are showing approximately 861sf of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area between the proposed DADU including roof area, driveway, walkway.  As such, drainage review is required. This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference / when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  Please ensure that you are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates (when applicable and if not already included in the complete plan set) and/or standard plan notes.  Please note that even if drainage review is not required, a completed Standard Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan is required to be included in the complete plan set when there is any ground disturbance.  As a separate review document upload the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable.  As part of the complete plan set, please submit the following: A completed Standard Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan.  Please replace with what you have now on sheet C-200 as that plan sheet is not complete.   A completed Standard Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan including the Site and Drainage Control Summary from On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator.  As a separate upload, please also submit a PDF of the entire completed On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator for review and retention. Subject: Side Sewers
Comment: DWC Plan: Because you intend to reuse the existing side sewer, an Evaluation and Certification of the existing side sewer by a Professional Engineer is required.  The PE Eval/Cert is not required if the existing side sewer was permitted and constructed after 2003.   See SMC 21.16.240 and Director's Rule 4-2011, "Requirements for Design & Construction of Side Sewers (Drainage & Wastewater Discharges)" for the requirements for the reuse of an existing side sewer. In summary, a licensed civil engineer must evaluate and certify the existing side sewer as follows: 1) If the side sewer is 50 years old or older, the side sewer will need to be lined.   2) If the existing side sewer is less than 50 years old, the side sewer must either be lined or the Evaluation and Certification process must pass a pressure test.   DR 4-2011 is available on the Side Sewer Permit webpage at http://www.seattle.gov/sdci/permits/permits-we-issue-(a-z)/side-sewer-permit.  On the Side Sewer Permit webpage, scroll down to "Steps to Get Your Permit" and expand "Research". Please revise General Note 1 to state that the existing side sewer to be reused must be Evaluated and Certified by a Professional Engineer and either rehabilitated (i.e. lined) or pressure tested all the way to the public mainline in the street in accordance with SMC 21.16.240 and Director's Rule 4-2011. The completed Evaluation and Certification form must be submitted to the Site Inspector during construction as part of the Side Sewer Permit inspections.  The form is also available on the Side Sewer Permit webpage.5 (3)

Subject: Drainage Review
Comment: According to City Records, the 12" storm pipe coming from 11740 Greenwood Ave N conveys the overflow from the detention tank which collects runoff from a catch basin and the roof downspouts for all of the roof.  I have researched City records as much as possible and the only information available is that shown on side sewer card 4340-14.  The location of the outfall for this pipe needs to be investigated.  The infiltration investigation for this property showed an infiltration rate of 0.25 in/hr so it is unlikely that discharge from the pipe is infiltrating.  One possible scenario is that the pipe extends all the way to the culvert in Phinney Ave N.  This needs to be investigated since having the pipe outfall under the new driveway will not be allowed. Please investigate the status of the pipe and depending on the outcome show one of the following on the plans: 1) If the 12" pipe ends on the property, the project shall extend the pipe so that it discharges to the ditch and culvert system in Phinney Ave N.   2) If the 12" pipe currently extends across the property and currently discharges to the ditch and culvert system, please show and identify this on the plan. The current easement extends across the entire property (not just in accordance with the side sewer card) so no changes are needed to the easement.  Please show the easement extending along the entire property on the plan.6 (1)

Subject: Infiltration BMPs
Comment: The infeasibility for infiltrating facilities is not clear. There appears to be room for an infiltrating facility in between the DADU and the SFR or between the SFR and the 30th Ave W ROW. The Drainage report indicates that the test was completed at elevation 225. It appears that the driveway proposed grade is between 228 and 225. If locating an infiltration trench only for the DADU at the upper end of the driveway it is not clear why this infiltration test is not showing that this can be feasible. It only must be shown that the minimum vertical setbacks can be met for hard pan or groundwater. It is also not clear why the SFR could not discharge to an infiltration trench at the west end of the property adjacent to the ROW. There is no required setback from the ROW and a subsurface investigation could be conducted to confirm that the vertical setbacks could be met.  If this proposed configuration is proposed, a simple test is only required (less than 2,000 Sf to a single facility).  Provide additional information to confirm why infiltration is not feasible other than what is described in the Drainage Report that a test cannot be conducted onsite.

The subsurface explorations presented in the uploaded geotechnical report lack sufficient detail to determine the site class. Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped steep slope and landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs).     Revegetation requirements apply within steep slope and landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within steep slope and landslide prone ECAs: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements for steep slope and landslide prone ECAs have not been met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.   1. Add note stating: Planting selections shall be Pacific Northwest native species suited to specific site conditions/orientation, no cultivars or hybrids are allowed.    2. Add note stating: New trees must be 4-6 feet in height and shrubs one-gallon size.  3. Show the following information consistently across all plan sheets:  A highly visible and durable protective barrier to prevent access and to protect steep slope environmentally critical areas (ECAs). Subject: Special Inspector nomination
Comment: Please address the following correction item from 7020767-CN. SMC 22.170.110.A.1. Based on test pit logs presented in the Geotechnical report, dated June 26, 2024, competent bearing soils were generally encountered at about Elevation 231 feet, with the exception of northwest portion of the site. Test pits TP-2 and TP-3 in the southern portions of the site encountered up to 8 feet of LOOSE fill soils. Caving was observed in both of these two test pits, indicating a LOOSE condition.  However, based on plan sheets A1.00 and A1.01, the block walls are shown to bear on structural fill placed over up to 12 feet of LOOSE fill soils (based on information from test pits TP-2 and TP-3). In addition, some elevation views show additional weight (significant thickness of structural fill and structures) will be added to the slope, increasing the hazard of future earth movement given the underlying loose soil conditions. The ECA code requirement is that the proposed development meets complete stabilization. Upload an addendum to the geotechnical report that includes methods that demonstrate complete stabilization for the final grading condition, particularly on the southern project area. Include supporting calculations and evaluations to demonstrate complete stabilization in the addendum, and update the plan set accordingly.ECA GeoTech (3)

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: Based on measurements of the proposed DADU floor plans, it appears to exceed Gross Floor Area (GFA) limits. Per Table A letter f for SMC 23.44.041, the gross floor area of a detached accessory dwelling unit may not exceed 1,000 square feet excluding garage and exterior-only accessed storage areas, covered porches and covered decks that are less than 25 square feet in area, and gross floor area that is underground. Up to 35 square feet of floor area dedicated to long-term bicycle parking shall be exempt from the gross floor area calculation for a detached accessory dwelling unit. Update the plans to include gross floor area diagrams and calculations for the structure that demonstrate compliance with Table A for 23.44.041, letter F. GFA should be measured from the interior face of the exterior walls (see Director ’s Rule 4-2019, https://www.seattle.gov/dpd/codes/dr/DR2019-4.pdf ). The GFA diagrams and calculations should account for the attached garage as exempt gross floor area in accordance with Table A for SMC 23.44.041. Any raised covered porch/patio/deck/entry in excess of 25 square feet should be counted toward GFA. If 25 square feet or less, such covered porches/patios/decks/entries should be identified as exempt.

If proceeding with option a or c above, the following will also require attention:  i. The plans propose two new driveways. Per 23.54.030.D.3, no portion of a driveway, whether located on a lot or on a right-of- way, shall exceed a slope of 15 percent, except as provided in 23.54.030.D.3. Update the plans to label driveway slope to demonstrate compliance with SMC 23.54.030.D.3. If proceeding with option c above, the following will also require attention: i. The plans propose 2 new curb cuts. Per SMC 23.54.030.F.1.c.1), The minimum distance between any two curb cuts located on a lot is 30 feet. Update the plans to demonstrate compliance with SMC 23.54.030.F.1.c.1).  ii. The plans propose 2 new curb cuts. Per SMC 23.54.030.G (and note 5 in SDOT Tip 2204 (See Tip 2204: http://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDOT/CAMs/cam2204.pdf), update the plans to show sight triangles on the plans, paying close attention to SMC 23.54.030.G.3, sight triangles shall be kept clear of obstructions in the vertical spaces between 32 inches and 82 inches from the ground. Please note that the sight triangles begin at the edge of the sidewalk to ensure visibility of existing and entering cars and pedestrians (see Exhibit E for 23.54.030). Obstructions include things such as retaining walls, fences, vegetation, etc.

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The provided lot coverage calculations are unverifiable based on the provided plans. Please address the following lot coverage items:  a. The plans do not label or dimension the eaves and gutters of the existing residence. It is unclear if these projections are being exempt or counted toward lot coverage appropriately. Per SMC 23.44.010.D.2.f, the first 36 ” of eaves and gutters that project from principal and accessory structures are exempt from lot coverage. Update the plans to label and dimension the eaves and gutters on both structures and exempt the appropriate areas from the calculations.  b. The lot coverage diagram appears count the eaves and gutters on the outside of the wall plane created by the covered patio posts toward lot coverage. The outer most side of the posts that support the covering should be used to determine the wall plane. The roof area that projects past that wall plane would be considered the eaves/gutters for purposes of applying the exemptions in SMC 23.44.010.D. The lot coverage diagram and site plan should clearly label these posts and dimension the projections past them the same as all other eave and gutter projections. Update the lot coverage diagram and  calculations accordingly.  c. The lot size used to determine maximum lot coverage is inconsistent with the provided survey. Update the lot coverage calculations to use the lot size as stated on the provided survey.

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential

However, parts of the DADU appear to exceed base height that are not otherwise a pitched, butterfly, or shed roof nor do they appear to meet any of the allowed projections in the footnotes of Table A for SMC 23.44.041. Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: Correction 1: General Information  This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped **steep slope and potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers.       Revegetation requirements apply within **steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been *met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.    Correction 2: Existing Conditions Sheet  (A1.1) 1. Provide an existing conditions plan. Clearly show the ** steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs and their buffers on the existing conditions plan.  Public facing GIS mapping tool, helpful for viewing property and generating a site plan with required information: ArcGIS Web Application  2. Provide a brief description/identification of the existing ground coverage (prior to work done without permits) within the area of temporary and permanent disturbance in the ECA. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping (vegetation species), blackberry or other invasive species, tree species, patio, pathway, driveway, stairway, etc. Calculate the area in square footage and show this on the existing conditions plan.  3. Show locations of all existing trees located within and adjacent to the disturbance area consistently across all plan view sheets. Include a tree table with genus, species, common name, DSH (diameter at standard height), dripline diameter and if trees/vegetation are proposed to remain or be removed. Please number trees consistently within table and across all plan view sheets. Do not include tier categories for trees in ECAs. 4. Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list of the existing ecological functions performed by the trees and vegetation within the ** steep slope and potential landslide prone ECA. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration (SMC 25.09.065.C.2.a). Revegetation (2)

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: Correction 3: Project Impacts (Proposed replanting plan) [25.09.065.C.2] Please provide a proposed site mitigation plan/table: Based on existing ground coverage, please show/delineate the proposed mitigation in the form of replanting. Determine the total area of impact that requires mitigation using the calculation (a+b=c):  a. Total new hard surface area  b. Total temporary construction disturbance area including all construction-related activities including, but not limited to construction access, staging area, temporary excavation, and areas of tree/vegetation removal.   c. Total area of impact that requires mitigation in the form of replanting.  Correction 4:  Proposed Mitigation  (Proposed replanting plan) 1. On the mitigation plan, show the location, size, species, quantities, and spacing of trees/shrubs to be newly planted. Use the ECA standard mitigation plan as a guide only.   a. Shrub quantities can be determined by using multiplier 0.042 times the total area of impact that requires mitigation.   b. Tree replacement quantities can be 1:1 or alternatively use an adjusted tree multiplier of 0.01 as the ECA standard mitigation plan multiplier results in an excessive number of trees. The goal is to provide a layered canopy. Seattle DPD Form - Standard Mitigation Plan c. References to help you choose native plants:  King County Native Plant Guide: Plant list - Native Plant Guide (kingcounty.gov),  WSU Native Plant Guide:WSU PNW Plants    2. Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list, an analysis of how the mitigation plan compensates for lost ecological functions within the ECA.   3. Add note stating: Planting selections shall be Pacific Northwest native species suited to specific site conditions/orientation, no cultivars or hybrids are allowed.    4. Add note stating: New trees must be 4-6 feet in height and shrubs one-gallon size.  5. Add note stating: Areas that have been cleared, graded, or compacted are to be amended with organic matter prior to planting. Mulch, such as wood chips, should be added to a 3 ” thickness over the entire planting area without covering the stems of plants.  6. Add note stating: The following monitoring and maintenance is required for a period of 5 years from date of plant installation. Self-monitoring is sufficient. No documentation is required to be submitted to SDCI unless requested.  a.  80 percent survival of new trees and vegetation planted at the end of five years;  b.  Annual inspections of the plants;  c.  Replacement of failed plants;  d.  Removal of exotic invasive species that have become established;   e. Photographic documentation of planting success retained for the five-year period; and  f. No permanent irrigation is allowed on steep slope areas or their buffers. Steep slope area only   Correction 5: Tree protection (A1.1, CSC) 1. Show the following information consistently across all plan view sheets:  a. A highly visible and durable protective barrier to prevent access and to protect steep slope environmentally critical areas (ECAs).   b. Tree/vegetation fence enclosing as much of the trees' driplines as possible using tree symbol [-o-o-o-].  c. Inner and outer root zones of all trees, with dimensions between tree trunks and tree/vegetation protective fence so workers and inspectors can accurately site them in the field.   Please add contact information (name, phone, email) for the project arborist to the plan set (if needed).

Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Subject: DWC
Comment: Sheet DWC: Repeated correction: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.

Subject: Replacement species
Comment: I strongly advise against planting both quaking aspen and Oregon ash.  Quaking aspen has an aggressive root system that can interfere with drainage and sewer pipes and spreads under patios and driveways.  Oregon ash is very susceptible to a pest that has recently arrived in our region (Emerald Ash borer) which has decimated ash populations in other parts of the country.  A better option would be Garry oak (Quercus garryana) a slow-growing but drought tolerant oak, scarlet oak, faster-growing but also drought-tolerant, or Spanish fir, a medium-sized evergreen.  Please choose one species.

Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs).       Revegetation requirements apply within potential landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within potential landslide prone ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.   1. Provide an existing conditions plan.    2. On the existing conditions plan, provide a brief description/identification of the existing ground coverage within the area of temporary and permanent disturbance in the ECA. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping (vegetation species), blackberry or other invasive species, tree species, patio, pathway, driveway, stairway, etc. Calculate the area in square footage and show this on the existing conditions plan.     3. Show locations of all existing trees located within and adjacent to the disturbance area consistently across all plan sheets with tree identifiers from the tree table on sheet L-1.0. Include on the tree table genus, species, dripline diameter and remove Tier category. Tier categories do not apply in ECA code, SMC25.09. Please number trees consistently within table and across all plan sheets.    4. On the existing conditions plan, provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list of the existing ecological functions performed by the trees and vegetation within the potential landslide prone ECA. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration (SMC 25.09.065.C.2.a). Subject: For Projects over 1,500 S.F.
Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2.1. Please submit the following with the next submittal: 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer.

Subject: Dimension Dispersion Facility Setbacks
Comment: Please add dimensions to the DWC plan demonstrating the minimum required setbacks below have been provided. Per the Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 3.1,  dispersion facilities (e.g. splash block, dispersion trench, transition zone) and the associated vegetated flow path, must meet the following horizontal setback requirements:  5 ’ from property lines parallel to flow path (except for property lines fronting the public right-of-way), 5 ’ from buildings without basements, and 10 ’ from buildings with basements, 10' from end of flow path to property line (except for property lines fronting the public right-of-way).

The Seattle Stormwater Manual and all of the templates and documents mentioned above are available at http://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code. The CSC/SOIL Plan and DWC Plan must be combined with the submitted Plan Set PDF.

Subject: DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F.
Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must demonstrate that all runoff up to the 25-year recurrence interval is infiltrated on-site, or, if not feasible, all runoff is dispersed on-site using a dispersion BMP per the Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer***. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer***.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer***. ***Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director. Subject: Seismic Site Class justification
Comment: The uploaded geotechnical report assumed Site Class D to determine seismic coefficients. To categorize the site as Site Class D, please demonstrate one of the following criteria: a) Shear wave velocity for the top 100 ft is between 600 and 1,200 ft/s. b) SPT-N blow counts for the top 100 ft are between 15 and 50 per foot. c) Undrained shear strength for the top 100 ft is between 1,000 and 2,000 lb/ft². The subsurface explorations presented in the uploaded geotechnical report lack sufficient detail to determine the site class. As per Section 11.4.3 of ASCE 7-16, when soil properties are not known in sufficient detail to determine the site class, Site Class D is selected as the default site class, and the value of Fa shall not be less than 1.2.  Please revise the seismic design parameters in the geotechnical report and update the structural design calculations accordingly.

Comment: Shear Wall H/L Adjustment Factors S-2.X Calcs 16 & 17 SDPWS 4.3.3 Clarify how the shear wall capacities/stiffness/force distribution have been adjusted for their stiffness for walls sharing force in a line. S2.0 SW107 Please include calculations for SW105 &107, as they  appear to be FTAO have piers that need to have reductions based on stiffness. Based on our design, the unit shear within the full height panels for shearwall 105 and 107(310 plf and 365 plf, respectively) are within acceptable tolerances to be considered proportional to their capacity (both are 3" on center edge nailing).  Therefore it is our professional opinion that the distribution of shear force within this shear line meets the intent of the NDS and no further action is required. Subject: Engineered Lateral
Comment: Overturning Calculation and no holdown at SW 202 Calcs 13 This comment is for reference and no response is required. It is made because the calculation shown appears to be non-conservative for walls with H/L>1.0. The calculations of forces in the wall show an addition of a horizontal force to the vertical force, and the force applied Emh does not appear to be correlated to E (possible issue with the spreadsheet). The OT calcs do not appear to follow the principles of statics with horizontal forces added to vertical forces. Please clarify how the forces have been added considering he locations directions of forces. Response Per ASCE 7-16 Section 12.14.3.2, Em = Emh + Ev  Emh is the effect of a horizontal seismic force, not the actual horizontal force in the wall. The horizontal force causes a vertical force at the end of a wall due to a moment couple. The principles of statics apply as a vertical force is being added to another vertical force. Cycle 2 The calculations do not follow the principles of statics per the original comment and our conference call on 7/7. Repeat comment. Include each force as a vector.

Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including a completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Subject: Administration
Comment: Revised Code of Washington (RCW) 64.55.005 requires that the developers of multi-unit residential buildings comply with one of the three options listed below. Indicate which option will be used and provide electronic copies of the required documents as specified. Option 1: a) Submit plans, details, and specifications for the construction of the building enclosure, per RCW 64.55.010(2). The building enclosure design documents must be signed and sealed by an architect or engineer licensed in the State of Washington, per RCW 64.55.10(3). b) Provide a statement on the plans or in a letter, signed and stamped as above, in substantially the following form: "The undersigned has provided building enclosure documents that in my professional judgment are appropriate to satisfy the requirements of RCW 64.55.005 through 64.55.090. ” c) Submit to the building inspector, a letter signed by a third-party qualified inspector certifying that the building enclosure has been inspected during construction and has been constructed in substantial compliance with the building enclosure design documents, per RCW 64.55.060. A final inspection will not be approved, nor a final certificate of occupancy issued prior to the receipt of the signed letter. Option 2: Submit a completed, signed, and recorded Condominium Sales Prohibition Covenant which prohibits the sale of individual dwelling units as condominiums for a minimum of five years. The completed and signed form must be recorded with the King County Recorder ’s office and submitted prior to permit issuance, per RCW 64.55.020(10). Option 3: Demonstrate RCW 64.55 does not apply by submitting an approved and recorded unit lot subdivision, prior to issuance of the construction permit.

Subject: PE Evaluation & Certification Required
Comment: If you intend to reuse existing side sewer, an Evaluation and Certification of the existing side sewers by a Professional Engineer is necessary because the existing side sewer/s were installed prior to 2004.   SS Code 21.16.240 and the Requirements for Design and Construction of Side Sewers Director's Rule (DR 4-2011) detail the requirements for use of an existing side sewer. In summary, a civil engineer must evaluate and certify the existing side sewer; if the side sewer is 50 years or older, the side sewer will need to be lined; if the existing side sewer is less than 50 years old, the side sewer must either be lined or the Evaluation and Certification process must include a pressure test. Please add  a very clear, boxed note added to the Drainage and Wastewater Control Plan that  the existing side sewer must be Evaluated and Certified by a Professional Engineer and either rehabilitated (i.e. lined) or pressure tested all the way to the public mainline in the street.  The completed Evaluation and Certification form must be submitted to the inspector during construction.  The form is available with the following link: http://www.seattle.gov/dpd/permits/permittypes/sidesewer/default.htm

Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Comment: Sheet A1.3: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. Comment: SMC 22.170.130. Nominate a geotechnical engineering firm on the SDCI Geotechnical Special Inspections Schedule form. The form  is named as " Special Inspection Notification" and can be found on the project portal. This form must be signed by the owner or owner's representative; the form cannot be signed by the contractor nor the geotechnical engineer.      The Inspection Agency must be the same engineer/firm that prepared the geotechnical report. If the owner nominates a different engineer/firm to act as the Geotechnical Special Inspector, the new engineer must review the original geotechnical report and submit a letter indicating a review was performed, along with a statement of agreement with the evaluation and provisions contained in the report. If the new engineer does not agree with aspects of the report, rebuttal evaluations and recommendations must be included in the review letter. The plans must be revised accordingly and submitted to SDCI for review. Please do not fill in special inspection items on the enclosed form.    Requests for changes of Special Inspection Agency that occur during plan review should be submitted with corrected plans. If the request occurs after permit issuance, send the materials to the geotechnical reviewer.

Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Comment: It appears tree #8 is considered to present a hazard per the arborist report. SDCI can approve removal based on the risk assessment section of Directors rule 07-2024: RISK ASSESSMENT As part of a development permit application, trees that meet Tier 2 tree designation are not regulated as Tier 2 trees when SDCI finds that the tree should be removed based on a risk assessment produced by a registered tree service provider who is currently credentialed with an ISA Tree Risk Assessment Qualification. The risk assessment must document that the tree is considered a High Risk hazard or that the tree has little or no likelihood of survival after construction. In making this determination, the registered tree service provider must consider crown size, structure, disease, past maintenance practice, potential damage to existing or future targets, risk mitigation options, proposed demolition and construction methods, and the likelihood of survival after construction. Tree service providers conducting commercial tree work on these trees must comply with the tree service provider registry requirements of SMC Chapter 25.11 Subsection 25.11.100. The replacement requirements of SMC Chapter 25 Subsection 25.11.090 apply. The arborist needs to update the report or provide an arborist memo that photo documents the tree condition.
