Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project. Subject: DWC
Comment: Sheet C2.0: The approved point of discharge for drainage for the proposed project is the ditch and culvert system on the far side of 40th Ave NE. It appears that due to the topography it is impossible to construct a piped discharge to the far side ditch or culvert that complies with the minimum requirements of the Seattle Department of Transportation regarding gravity flow and minimum cover. There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal: 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer.Drainage (3)

Please see the following requirements for the project with no off site point of stormwater discharge:  There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. These notes and requirements are in lieu of establishing a formalized seasonal grading restriction on the project and constitute the customary requirements that would be instituted for a seasonal grading extension:   A site visit from the Geotechnical Special Inspector shall occur during each day of active grading and in the event of significant rainfall which might compromise stabilization measures between November 1 and March 31. However, as a minimum standard, the Geotechnical Special Inspector is required to conduct a site visit if more than one-half inch of precipitation occurs on any given day. Any recommendations required to maintain stability of excavations and proper functioning of the sediment/erosion control system provided by the Geotechnical Special Inspector and SDCI personnel shall be implemented immediately.  The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide copies of field reports to SDCI Site Development Services Section no later than 48 hours after each inspection. Subject: Engineered Lateral
Comment: Outstanding Cycle 1 Comment: ASCE 7-16 12.1.2 - If using the dead loads that are within a light-framed shear wall to help reduce net uplift at the shear wall end, SDCI will accept using a tributary length of the shear wall that is the least of the following: a) half the total shear wall length; b) the shear wall height between stories; c) for FTAO or perforated shear wall, the distance from the shear wall end to midspan of the header of the nearest wall opening. Demonstrate that the portion of each shear wall assumed as contributing to resisting end uplift does not exceed this limit.  Alternatively, submit calculations justifying that the shear wall construction has adequate strength and rigidity to transfer dead loads from a greater tributary length. Additionally, it is unclear if appropriate load combinations are being used for calculation of overturning and resisting moments. Please revise shear wall calculations using the appropriate loads and load combinations for resisting overturning and provide holdowns as required.  Cycle 2 additional comments: Please provide a rational analysis demonstrating the shear walls act as rigid bodies for the purposes of transferring distributed dead load to the end of the wall and resiting overturning. SDCI agrees that this is an acceptable means of compliance, however calculations were not provided. The recommended dead load maximums are provided to not require rational analysis. Primary concern is walls with large openings, such as grid 1. Where multiple wall types utilize the same calculation, please provide a sample calculation for the worst case scenario describing load paths, demands and capacities to expedite review.Derek Ohlgren (4)

Subject: Engineered Lateral
Comment: Outstanding Cycle 1 comment: AWC SDPWS 4.3.2: The wood shearwalls appear to use the FTAO or perforated method for calculating shearwall capacity. Please provide these calculations instead of calculations based on overall wall length. Cycle 2 comment: FTAO calculations were not provided. Please provide calculations. A quick check of SW103A using the APA FTAO calculator indicated that panel edge nailing of 4" o.c. may be required.  FTAO may not be applicable for this wall due to the limited height above the window compromising the rigidity of the transfer panel. In the provided calculation (see snip at right) for SW 103A the total wall length of 11ft is used, with 8ft contributing. This is the appropriate value for the two individual qualifying wall piers. When individual piers are used a holdown is required at each pier. However the full length of the wall was used for the holdown calculation, indicating that FTAO was used for the shearwall calculation. FTAO typically requires additional nailing to transfer the forces around the opening. Please reconcile this difference and either provide a) holdowns at the end of each wall segment or b)increased nailing to meet the requirements of FTAO.

Subject: Subgrade and bearing pressure
Comment: SMC 22.170.110 A.1.  Based on subsurface information and recommendations presented in the geotechnical report by Riley Group dated January 31, 2025  as well as desired bottom of footing elevations, it appears that the eastern portion of the proposed development will be supported on footing founded where the loose silty sand was encountered in the exploration, B-1 up to 10 feet bgs. However, the geotechnical report recommended that the proposed structure be supported on conventional footings bearing on undisturbed soil, or on properly compacted structural fill. The geotechnical report further stated that the level 2 foundations that extend east requires loose soil overexcavation and backfilled with structural fill. Please revise the plan to include  (1) a foundation design and/or footing subgrade improvement that shows how the proposed development will be supported on the competent bearing soil and  (2) an excavation plan that shows extent and maximum cut slope conditions sufficient to expose competent bearing soil or elevation needed to improve footing subgrade that satisfies the recommendations presented in the geotechnical report.

If the new engineer does not agree with aspects of the report, rebuttal evaluations and recommendations must be included in the review letter. The plans must be revised accordingly and submitted to SDCI for review. Requests for changes of Special Inspection Agency that occur during plan review should be submitted with corrected plans. Subject: General
Comment: General Drainage Review Information: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload a PDF of the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable.
